LESSON: READING COMPREHENSION

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: GERMAN
Strand: READING Theme 2. Family Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested L
Topic 2.3: Reading Comprehension

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading Comprehension. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why is reading important?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. read texts for language learning
2. appreciate the importance of reading texts fluently
3. identify German sounds for articulation
4. read aloud German sounds for articulation
5. value the role of articulation in communication
6. identify vocabulary in reading for fluency
7. recognize the role of fluency in a language
8. read short simple texts for enjoyment

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING COMPREHENSION
Subject: GERMAN · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading Comprehension helps you succeed in GERMAN. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING COMPREHENSION
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Read texts for language learning

What this means
In this part you learn to read texts for language learning. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: read texts for language learning.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading Comprehension”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can read texts for language learning. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Appreciate the importance of reading texts fluently

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the importance of reading texts fluently. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the importance of reading texts fluently.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading Comprehension to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the importance of reading texts fluently. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Identify German sounds for articulation

What this means
In this part you learn to identify German sounds for articulation. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify German sounds for articulation.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify German sounds for articulation. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Read aloud German sounds for articulation

What this means
In this part you learn to read aloud German sounds for articulation. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: read aloud German sounds for articulation.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading Comprehension”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can read aloud German sounds for articulation. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 5: Value the role of articulation in communication

What this means
In this part you learn to value the role of articulation in communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: value the role of articulation in communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading Comprehension to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can value the role of articulation in communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 6: Identify vocabulary in reading for fluency

What this means
In this part you learn to identify vocabulary in reading for fluency. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify vocabulary in reading for fluency.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify vocabulary in reading for fluency. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading Comprehension is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading Comprehension”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: read texts for language learning)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading Comprehension to a partner. (skill: appreciate the importance of reading texts fluently)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: identify German sounds for articulation)

Example 4: Read a short paragraph about “Reading Comprehension”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: read aloud German sounds for articulation)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading Comprehension to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: read texts for language learning.
3. Practise this skill: appreciate the importance of reading texts fluently.
4. Practise this skill: identify German sounds for articulation.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Reading Comprehension from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading Comprehension: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study Reading Comprehension?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is reading important?
2. Why is reading aloud important?
3. How do we become fluent in a language?
4. How do we get all the needed information from a reading text?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading Comprehension means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: read texts for language learning.
5. Be able to: appreciate the importance of reading texts fluently.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
